name: Edgar Carbone
life: “I still remember my old schoolteacher mocking a single soft vowel.” People around Tideline Market know Edgar by a small Saturday habit. Edgar picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I corrected her accent too often. I sounded exactly like the teacher who frightened me at her age.
appearance: Edgar has a long silver braid, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. When somebody else has the floor, Edgar grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Edgar reads little signals of discomfort very accurately and has an unfortunate habit of overruling people for their own good. The friends who say stop are the ones Edgar trusts most.
agenda: To replace corrections with an invitation.
family: Lara Finch is Edgar’s cousin raised in the same household. Edgar leaves the first voice message. Lara calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A call heard twice*, Lara says, “I supervise the desk. I was about to post a single staff photograph before I checked the two time entries.”
connections: Cara Carvalho (grandchild). A grandparent practicing listening can stay in the room when the child changes languages.

reactions.situation: A grandparent tries to correct a word in front of classmates
reactions.response: Edgar asks the grandparent to save the correction until the pupil asks for it.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
